'''Semelai''' is an [[Austroasiatic language]] spoken in the Malay Peninsula by [[Semelai people]]. It belongs to the [[Southern Aslian languages|Southern]] branch of the [[Aslian language]] subgrouping.  The Semelai people reside predominantly around the Bera, Serting and associated river systems in the states of [[Pahang]], [[Negeri Sembilan]] and [[Johor]].

Semelai is a [[split ergative]] language motivated by semantics and [[word order]] shift.{{sfn|Kruspe|2004a|pp=5-6}}

* Stops {{IPA|/p t c k/}} are heard as {{IPA|[p̚ t̚ c̚ k̚]}} word-final position.
* Palatal sounds {{IPA|/c ɟ/}} are slightly affricated as {{IPA|[cᶝ ɟᶽ]}} when in word-initial position.
* {{IPA|/s/}} may occur as {{IPA|[s]}} or {{IPA|[ɕ]}} within free variation.
* Nasals {{IPA|/m n ɲ ŋ/}} can occur as prestopped {{IPA|[ᵇm ᵈn ᶡɲ ᶢŋ]}} when in word-final position.
* {{IPA|/r/}} can be heard as {{IPA|[ɾ]}} when in word-final position. When preceded by a nasal {{IPA|/n/}} it is heard as {{IPA|[ᵈr]}}.
* {{IPA|/w, j/}} are heard as off-glides {{IPA|[ʷ, ʲ]}} when in word-final position. After nasal vowels, they are then heard as nasalized {{IPA|[ʷ̃, ʲ̃]}}.

==Morphosyntax==
Semelai has many inchoative verbs such as ''rmɔl'' "to be male", ''hitam'' "be black", which at the first glance may hint a flexible language like nearby [[Austronesian languages]]. However, the vast majority of Semelai lemmas can be identified unproblematically to a particular word category. Verbs and nouns must undergo [[Morphological derivation|derivation]] via infixation or prefixation in order to function as other lexical categories, eg. ''rlmɔl'' "male" → ''rmɔl'' "to be male", ''yɔk'' "take" → ''nk-yɔk'' "taking INF". Loan words from Austronesian are mostly precategorial, eg. ''tuŋkɒt'' "a stick, to prop up".{{sfn|Kruspe|2004a|p=95}} The language recognizes several distinct [[parts of speech]] that are morphologically and syntactically distinguished: the superclass nominal (which includes nouns as an open word class); [[verb]]; [[Expressives|expressive]]; [[preposition]]; [[adverb]]; auxiliary; existential and ascriptive predicators; negator; connective; [[interjection]].{{sfn|Kruspe|2004a|p=94}}
